key_step: Telescoping the two integrals via $x^{6+i}-x^{3+i}=x^{3+i}(x^3-1)$, then triangular determinant and $|adj(A^{-1})|=|A|^{-2}$
justification: Spotting the cancellation is one easy trick; the rest is a triangular determinant and a standard adjoint identity, a routine chain of three standard results with no real insight. Same level as the integral-equation chain 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

key_step: Pull $\sin x$ out of the integral so $f=x+A\sin x$; solve for the constant $A$
justification: Separable-kernel integral equation: one standard idea followed by an integration by parts and a linear equation for $A$. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2), integral equation solved by routine steps; options let the student check.

key_step: Split at the breakpoints of $[2x]$ and $|x|$ and integrate piecewise
justification: Single familiar move (piecewise integration of greatest-integer and modulus), tiny arithmetic. Close to 2021-P2-Q11 (L1), a direct integral evaluation; numerical format keeps it from being 0.

chapter: Indefinite Integration - Differentiation under the identity / Monotonicity
key_step: Differentiate both sides to cancel $g$ and get $g'=\cos x-\sin x$, then judge four monotonicity statements
justification: Two linked ideas (derivative identity with an unknown function, then monotonicity of $g$, $g'$, $g\pm g'$) and four statements each needing a genuine sign check, with several traps. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q7 (L3, implications needing checks).

key_step: $x=\cos\theta$ gives $\tan\frac\theta2$, then $\int\sec\theta\,d\theta$; evaluate and simplify the log
justification: A routine chain: trigonometric substitution, half-angle simplification, secant integral, constant from $g(1)=0$ and log simplification to match the option. No unfamiliar idea; the exact-value simplification is the only slip risk. Level of 2024-P2-Q16 (L2).

key_step: Rewrite the rational factor as $\varphi+\varphi'$ so that $\int e^x(\varphi+\varphi')=e^x\varphi$, then differentiate thrice
justification: A very familiar pattern, but the splitting needs a few algebraic steps and then three derivatives; routine chain without insight, so L2 rather than L1. Similar demand to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

key_step: King property to remove $1+e^x$, then $\sin^6+\cos^6$ and $t=\tan2x$ over $(0,\infty)$
justification: Three standard tricks in a row (king property with $e^x$, $\sin^6+\cos^6$ reduction, tan substitution to an infinite-limit arctan), each familiar; chain length lifts it above 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) to L2, similar to 2024-P2-Q16 (L2).

key_step: Recognise the Riemann sum $\int_0^1\frac{dx}{(1+x^2)(1+x)}$ and do partial fractions
justification: Riemann-sum recognition and a standard partial-fraction integral; multi-step but routine and options allow a check. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2); not Level 3 since no second idea is linked.

key_step: King property $x\to\pi-x$ makes the $e^{\pm\cos x}$ factors add to 1
justification: One familiar move (king property with $e^{c}/(e^c+e^{-c})$) followed by a one-line substitution. Same demand as 2026-P2-Q4 (L1), king property on $\frac{1}{3^x+3}$.

key_step: Form $b_n-b_{n-1}$ via $\cos^2A-\cos^2B$ so $\sin x$ cancels, then test the A.P./G.P. options
justification: The key idea (take consecutive differences and use product-to-sum) is a known pattern for integral recurrences but not a one-liner; the rest is a standard integral and checking four A.P./G.P. options. Roughly the demand of 2021-P2-Q3 (L2).
